source_snapshot.criteria: All information should match SPEC definition.
source_snapshot.deepseek: NO; BIOS Advanced -> Performance page must be viewed by an operator and compared with SPEC.

historical_reviews.deepseek: The manual boundary is correct, but its concise instruction does not define the complete field oracle, dynamic-value semantics or preserved evidence.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Classification and read-only controls are accepted; the field matrix, platform identity, optional/dynamic handling and no-mutation boundary are retained.
historical_reviews.history: Exact source-key and code searches found no duplicate variant or earlier completed record; this row is separate from functional benchmark, stress or tuning tests.
historical_reviews.v3_1: A page named Performance can expose policy, limit, telemetry or capability values, but this source only requests information comparison; it does not authorize changing settings or claiming measured workload performance.

original_test_intent: Have a qualified operator inspect every requested field and sub-option on the BIOS Advanced Performance page and compare the displayed information with the owner-approved platform specification.
original_method: Verify SUT and BIOS/AGESA identity plus the complete expected field matrix; enter the Performance page read-only, capture each displayed label/value and platform-dependent absence, compare field by field using approved static or dynamic semantics, preserve logs and exit without changing settings.
manual_activity: A qualified operator verifies the exact platform and firmware, traverses the BIOS Performance page, captures every required label/value and compares it with the approved field matrix without making a change.
required_inputs: Exact SUT, board, CPU and BIOS/AGESA identity
Owner-approved complete Performance page field/value matrix
Static, dynamic, optional, hidden and unsupported field semantics
Approved tolerance or capture-state rule for any dynamic value
Qualified BIOS operator and read-only access
Redaction policy and expected acceptance matrix
safety_requirements: Treat the page as read-only and do not alter CPU, memory, boost, power, thermal, fan or workload settings
Do not infer benchmark or stress-test coverage from the page title
Do not clear dmesg, syslog or SEL
Capture operating state and timestamp for any dynamic field
Stop on an unexpected writable change, warning, unsafe thermal/power state or ambiguous field
agent_execution_scope: Prepare the field-by-field oracle and evidence checklist
Support read-only SUT, firmware and optional OS telemetry capture
Do not claim BIOS UI control or replace the operator's page evidence
Compare captured values with the approved static/dynamic/optional rules
Record mismatches and ambiguity without assigning PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED
engineer_actions: Approve the complete field matrix and semantics
Confirm the intended capture state and tolerance for dynamic values
Resolve discrepancies and own PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: NO/manual is correct because the authoritative evidence is the BIOS Performance page; its prose is a human instruction, not an executable agent command.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Manual operator: verify target and firmware identity, enter Advanced -> Performance read-only, capture every requested field, compare each with the approved matrix and exit without saving any change.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Advanced -> Performance, information check and 20/20-minute estimates remain; destructive log clearing is prohibited and no benchmark workload is added.

modernized_recommendation.status: MANUAL READ-ONLY PERFORMANCE PAGE FIELD MATRIX
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a signed comparison matrix containing field label/path, expected value or rule, static/dynamic/optional status, capture state, observed value and evidence reference for every page item.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes the unspecified SPEC comparison auditable and prevents a page inspection from being misreported as a functional performance test.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Optional OS telemetry may corroborate platform state but cannot replace BIOS UI evidence; benchmark throughput, stress stability and tuning behavior are outside this row.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Firmware revisions can rename, hide or dynamically update fields, so acceptance needs version-specific semantics rather than guessed equivalence.

project_override_considerations: A Project may define additional Performance-page fields or dynamic tolerances, but must publish the version-bound matrix before execution. Any requested setting mutation, benchmark or stress run is a separately governed test and is not inherited from this row.
expected_evidence: Redacted SUT/board/CPU and BIOS/AGESA identity plus capture timestamp/state
Complete expected-versus-observed Performance page matrix with dynamic/optional semantics
Protected page captures covering every requested field and sub-option
Optional complete read-only OS telemetry explicitly marked supporting only
Mismatch, absent, extra, ambiguous and warning findings plus preserved relevant logs
No-mutation confirmation and engineer-owned PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Test Set, Procedure and Criteria consistently specify a read-only BIOS Advanced Performance information check. The broad page name and unspecified SPEC reduce readiness but do not create competing targets.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The manual workflow is safely defined once the owner supplies the complete version-specific field matrix, dynamic/optional rules, qualified operator and protected evidence path.

review_improvement: Turns a generic `check information` instruction into a complete version-bound, read-only field reconciliation while explicitly excluding unrequested tuning and benchmark claims.
independent_technical_reasoning: Displayed Performance values may represent capabilities, configured policy, limits or live telemetry. Correct comparison therefore depends on exact firmware identity and per-field semantics; a matching OS value is only corroboration and a page snapshot alone cannot prove workload performance.
